title: Photo tour: Paul Mares, Brunies, Rappolo, Sharkey, Monk Hazel, Fazola
summary: Mares describes the big photos on the wall, led by Paul and the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, with Brunies, Rappolo, Sharkey, Hazel and Fazola.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Someone call. Yeah. To continue, what I wanted to mention on the tape is that you have all of these pictures. It looks like a museum, a wonderful museum of the best collection I've seen of old photos, big and large ones. Let's walk around the room once and tell me something about some of these pictures, the different people.

Well, of course, facing us here, Bill, is the old New Orleans Rhythm Kings. Brother Paul was the leader of that outfit, which I think was the greatest white band to ever sit on a bandstand. That's not only my opinion. That's the opinion of a lot of the greats if you talk to them. And, of course, up here we've got Paul in the middle here.
I might mention that there's a big enlargement about three feet by two and a half or so. And all of these enlargements are around two by three feet or 18 by 14 or something, aren't they?
And that big picture up there is Paul. Paul, that's the Paul, 1920.

I noticed he's holding, not hurry too much, I want to look at that, he's holding a trumpet. What kind of a trumpet did he use? Do you remember anything about him? I don't remember, Bill. I guess it's a trumpet or it could have been a cornet.
It's a trumpet, no. He started out playing cornet, but in that particular picture there he's playing trumpet. It could have been a con, I think, because they were very famous in those days.
They were the most popular here. Yes. Now, on the left here we have a little tailgate himself, Georgie Brunas.
He's puffing his left cheek out. That's right. And on the right here, Paul, we have Leon Rupola, one of the real greats.
Just got a postcard today from someone in Chicago saying that George is opening a new place there now.
Well, George keeps going. He's always the same. In fact, I think he plays the same horn that he played. That is the instrument himself. He still has the same one he played in the early days.
Yeah, we had a nice idea with him last year. Of course, over here to the left is a picture of Sharky, one of New Orleans' real greats that's

left today in the Dixieland field. On the left over here we have Mark Hazel. In my opinion, probably one of the greatest Dixieland drummers in the business. Under him we have Fazola. In my opinion, another one of the real great clarinet players. Him and Rapp, probably the greatest white clarinet players that ever come out of New Orleans.
